title: Bitcoin AI Model Review — Week 43: 2 of 6 Calls Correct
meta_description: Week 43 graded: 2 of 6 Bitcoin calls correct (33%). All-time: 40.0% over 80 public calls. Paper portfolio +10.2% vs holding.

intro: This QuantAura Signals recap covers week 43 from 2026-10-18 to 2026-10-23.
The model had a poor showing, landing only 2 of 6 resolved calls correct for a 33.3 percent accuracy rate.
Despite four losses overall, the week closed on a brief hit streak of 2.
days: On Sunday, the model predicted sell with 74.1 percent confidence, but price moved up 0.43 percent.
Monday and Tuesday both brought hold signals at 81.8 percent and 61.3 percent confidence while price gained 1.15 percent and 1.71 percent.
Thursday marked a recovery as a hold call at 51.6 percent confidence matched a minus 0.28 percent price change.
Friday completed the week with a correct hold signal at 60.3 percent confidence during a minus 0.22 percent decline.
spotlight: The major miss occurred on Wednesday, 2026-10-21.
The model issued a buy call at 84.1 percent confidence, its highest certainty of the entire week.
Bitcoin dropped minus 3.23 percent over the 24 hour horizon instead.
This call was flatly wrong and stands as the worst prediction of the period.
trend: Market movement rose steadily across the first three days before dropping sharply midweek.
Model signals lagged behind this curve, staying cautious or short during the rise and buying right before the decline.
Late week action settled below the 1.0 percent flat band threshold, allowing hold calls to score hits.
portfolio: Starting with 10000.0 dollars over 82 days and 10 trades, the paper portfolio sits at 11014.61 dollars.
That equals a 10.15 percent return after accounting for 163.2 dollars in fees paid at 0.15 percent per side.
A simple buy and hold strategy reached 12446.37 dollars, producing a 24.46 percent gain.
Following the model signals lagged buy and hold by minus 14.32 percent, with the portfolio currently holding cash.
record: All time results stand at 32 hits and 48 misses out of 80 resolved calls, producing an overall accuracy of 40.0 percent.
Looking at the recent 30 day window across 28 resolved calls, accuracy is nearly identical at 39.3 percent.
By signal type, hold leads at 69.7 percent over 33 calls, buy achieves 30.0 percent over 20 calls, and sell sits at 11.1 percent over 27 calls.
With only 80 total resolved calls on record, this sample size remains small and must be evaluated with restraint.

research.title: High accuracy still is not a trading edge
paragraphs: Our own published measurements show something most channels hide. A model can score well on classification metrics and still not be profitable to trade after fees.
That finding is the reason this scoreboard exists in public.
So the paper portfolio sits next to the accuracy in these recaps, and the two numbers are allowed to disagree in front of you.
